summary: The root ضنن (Dnn) primarily means to be avaricious or stingy with something, to withhold it from others, or to grudge it.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: ضَنَّ بِهِ, (Mgh, Msb,) first pers. ضَنِنْتُ بِهِ, (S, Msb, *) [and one may say عَلَيْهِ, and عَنْهُ, in the place of بِهِ, (see ضَنِينٌ,)] and ضَنِنُوا occurs, in a verse of Kaanab Ibn-Umm-Sáhib, used by poetic license for ضَنُّوا, (S,) aor. ضَنَنَ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and ضَنَّ, (Msb,) first pers. ضَنَنْتُ, (S, Msb, *) aor. ضَنِنَ, (S, Msb, K,) accord to Fr, (S,) or, accord. to Th, Fr said, I have heard ضَنَنْتُ, though I have not heard أَضِنُّ, but this aor. is mentioned by Yaakoob; (TA;) inf.
اِضْطَنَّ (originally اِضْتَنَّ, TA) He (a man, TA) was, or became, niggardly, tenacious, stingy, or avaricious. (K.) [See also 1.]

ضِنٌّ an inf. n. of 1 [q. v.]. (S, &c.) Also A thing highly esteemed, of which one is tenacious. (TA.) [Hence] one says, هُوَ ضِنِّى He is the person of whose affection I am tenacious; as also and: (TA:) or he is my particular, or special, friend, (K, TA,) مِنْ بَيْنِ إِخْوَانِى [ chosen from among my brethren ]; (S, TA;) as though I appropriated him specially to myself, and were tenacious of him because of the place that he held in my estimation: as is said in the S, it is like special…
ضِنَّةٌ an inf. n. of ضَنَّ: (Msb:) or a subst. therefrom signifying Niggardliness, tenaciousness, stinginess, or avarice: (Mgh:) or vehement niggardliness &c.; as also. (TA.) See also ضِنٌّ.

ضَنِينٌ Niggardly, tenacious, stingy, or avaricious, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) بِشَىْءٍ [ of a thing ], (S,) or بِشَىْءٍ نَفِيسٍ [ of a thing held in high estimation ]. (TA.) وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ, in the Kur [lxxxi. 24], as some read it, others reading بِظَنِينٍ [q. v.], is expl. by Zj as meaning, And he is not a tenacious concealer of that which has been revealed to him: and if عَن or بِ were substituted for عَلَى, it would be correct. (TA.) See also 1. And see ضِنٌّ.

ضَنَانَةٌ an inf. of 1 [q. v.]. (S &c.) [Hence,] one says, هَجَمْتُ عَلَى القَوْمِ بِضَنَانَتِهِمْ, meaning (assumed tropical:) [ I came suddenly upon the people, or party, in their close state, i. e.,] when they had not dispersed themselves. (TA.) And أَخَ ْتُ الأَمْرَ بِضَنَانَتِهِ (assumed tropical:) [ I took to the affair ] in its fresh state. (TA.)
ضَنِينَةٌ; and its pl. ضَنَائِنُ: see ضِنٌّ.

مَضَنَّةٌ: see ضِنَّةٌ. هٰ َا عِلْقُ مَضَنَّةٍ and مَضِنَّةٍ [the former mentioned after the latter in the S] This is a thing held in high estimation, of which one is tenacious, (S, K, TA,) and for which people vie in desire. (TA.) [See also عِرْقٌ, last sentence.]

المَضْنُونُ a name of [ The compound of perfumes commonly called ] الغَالِيَةُ; (Ez-Zejjájee, S, K, TA;) as also; (Ez-Zejjájee, S, * TA;) which latter is said by As to be a sort of perfume; and so is the former in the A: in the M the former is said to be the oil of ben: it is thus called because one is tenacious of it. (TA.) Also, (IKh, TA,) or, (K, TA,) a name of The well Zemzem. (K, TA.)
المَضْنُونَةُ: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
